clue.text: One who is OTT in the theatre could present dilemma to star

definitions.text: One who is OTT in the theatre

indicators.note: the letters could be presented in a new order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ham actor could make a star's life a dilemma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could present' rearranges DILEMMATOSTAR into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who overacts, playing everything over the top, is a ham given to theatrical excess.

clue.text: Fancy an introduction to Norway's secret delights?

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or reworked, so the letters are rearranged
the introduction of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An invitation to discover the hidden pleasures of Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' rearranges AN, N (first of Norway's) and SECRET.
explanation.definitionFit: To delight someone is to enchant or captivate them, the verb sense here.

clue.text: Cat to jump with no small power

indicators.note: with no tells us a letter is taken away from the word before

parts.note: to pounce is to jump on prey
a lower-case p is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A big cat leaps but lacks strength.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard is also called the ounce, a large wild feline.

clue.text: Papers finally lodged in stacked-up box files

indicators.note: lodged in means placed inside the other piece
in a down clue stacked up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to spar is to box

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: Office papers end up inside a pile of filing boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'stacked-up' means the box synonym is read from bottom to top; 'files' is a noun for tools, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasp is a coarse kind of file used for smoothing wood or metal, so these are tools.

clue.text: Numbered group in endless confusion, we pontificate

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
endless removes the closing letter of the word

parts.note: a morass is a muddle or state of confusion
a list is a numbered set of items

explanation.surface: Self-righteous preachers admit their list of items is in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims the last letter from the confusion synonym; 'we pontificate' defines the answer as the preachers' own voice.
explanation.definitionFit: People who preach about right and wrong would say of themselves that they lecture others on ethics.

clue.text: Worked in an underground movement

parts.note: sounds like resistance work in wartime, but literally describes digging a passage beneath the ground

explanation.surface: Someone served with the secret resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Excavating a passage under the earth is literally making progress below the surface.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink making one shy

definitions.meaning: a gin-based cocktail, as in the Singapore variety
to shy is to throw or hurl, as with a slingshot

explanation.surface: A cocktail makes someone bashful.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a spirit-based mixed drink and the act of hurling something.

clue.text: A multi-faith alternative to baptism? It has advantages and disadvantages

definitions.meaning: a christening blessing from several religions at once would be mixed
the idiom for something both good and bad

explanation.surface: An interfaith ceremony is weighed for its pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something that brings benefits along with drawbacks.

clue.text: Fiendish sailor crosses the street protesting

indicators.note: crosses here means the street piece sits across the join, between the other two

parts.note: demon used as an adjective means fiendishly skilful or wicked
a rating is a non-officer sailor
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A wicked seaman walks across the road during a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiendish' stands for the adjectival use of demon, as in a demon bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Demonstrating means taking part in a public protest march or rally.

clue.text: Plans favoured by nurses

parts.note: in means fashionable or in favour
to tend is to nurse or look after

explanation.surface: Schemes popular with nursing staff.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend something is to plan or mean to do it.

clue.text: Man with cycle hurried in front of cows

indicators.note: in front of places the first piece before the second

parts.note: ran means hurried
kine is an archaic plural of cow

explanation.surface: A man on a bike races ahead of a herd of cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: William Rankine, Scottish engineer, gave his name to the Rankine thermodynamic cycle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rankine cycle, the steam-engine model, is named after this Victorian physicist.

clue.text: Get rid of article in language few of us can read

indicators.note: in places the article inside the language

parts.words: language few of us can read
parts.note: Erse is Scottish or Irish Gaelic, read by few
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Remove an item written in an obscure tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to remove or wipe out completely.

clue.text: Vocal exercise with only one repeated note keeping loud I love

indicators.note: keeping means holding the next piece inside

parts.note: sole means the only one
f (forte) means loud in music

indicators.note: repeated means the piece is written twice

parts.note: G is a musical note
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A singer's warm-up on a single note, sung loudly with affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeated' doubles the note; love is zero in tennis, which looks like O.
explanation.definitionFit: Solfeggio is a singing exercise using the sol-fa syllables.

clue.text: Is he the originator of "Bard-craft"? A trick!

definitions.text: Is he the originator of "Bard-craft"? A trick!

indicators.note: the originator of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle

explanation.surface: Was this man really the author behind Shakespeare's plays, or is the idea a hoax?
explanation.walkthrough: Some claim Francis Bacon wrote Shakespeare's plays; the clue mocks the theory as a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon is proposed by some as the real author of the Bard's works.

clue.text: This? Won't use Blair, being beaten — it's surprisingly done for!

definitions.text: This? Won't use Blair, being beaten — it's surprisingly done for!

indicators.note: being beaten means knocked about, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the anagram pool; taking away the letters of the following piece leaves the answer

explanation.surface: A party rebrand that refuses to use its leader, now defeated and finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of WONTUSEBLAIR are those of the answer plus ITS; 'done for' marks ITS as removed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Labour Party rebranded under Tony Blair from 1994, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Saint is seen around about churches

parts.note: St Basil the Great

indicators.note: around means the word is wrapped about the next piece

parts.note: ca (circa) means about

explanation.surface: A saint is seen wandering around the cathedrals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps only the second word around the Latin abbreviation for about (circa).
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large oblong church, often granted special papal privileges.

clue.text: Germans taking half the bunks on ships

indicators.note: half means only part of the word is kept

parts.note: berths are bunks on a ship or train
liners are large passenger ships

explanation.surface: German passengers grab half the beds aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: People from Berlin are inhabitants of Germany's capital, hence Germans.

clue.text: Banal piece by essayist? It's a gem

parts.note: corn is trite, sentimental material
Elian means by Elia, the pen-name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A trite essay turns out to be a jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornelian is a reddish semi-precious stone, a variety of chalcedony.

clue.text: Like a choir's turn away from the congregation?

definitions.text: Like a choir's turn away from the congregation?

parts.words: Like a choir's turn away from the congregation
parts.note: in a traditional church the altar is at the east end, so turning from the people faces that way

explanation.surface: Choristers turn their backs on the worshippers.
explanation.definitionFit: Churches are traditionally oriented with the altar to the east, toward which the choir would turn.

clue.text: Painter — one to live on (not English name)

indicators.note: not means these letters are left out

parts.note: an endurer is one who lasts or lives on
E for English and N for name

explanation.surface: An artist hopes to be remembered, but not under an English name.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing E and N from ENDURER leaves the German artist Albrecht Dürer.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was a German Renaissance artist and engraver.

clue.text: Country moans terribly about pouring rain

indicators.note: about means wrapping around the other piece
terribly means badly, so the letters are jumbled
pouring suggests a disordered rush, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles bitterly about the rain in some country.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'terribly' and 'pouring' signal anagrams; the jumbled rain sits inside the jumbled moans.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a tiny republic surrounded by Italy.

clue.text: One taken in by rogue, king goes out as one too trustful

indicators.note: taken in by means placed inside the next piece
goes out means this letter is removed

parts.note: a knave is a rogue
K is the chess abbreviation for king
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A gullible person is conned by a crook as the monarch departs.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping K from KNAVE leaves NAVE; I goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive describes someone innocent and credulous.

clue.text: Very happy as a cyclist, but not as a penny-farthing rider?

definitions.text: Very happy as a cyclist, but not as a penny-farthing rider?

parts.words: Very happy as a cyclist, but not as a penny-farthing rider
parts.note: walking ... means elated, and modern bikes ride on pneumatic tyres while penny-farthings had solid ones

explanation.surface: Modern cyclists are cheerful; Victorian riders less so.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom walking on air means elated, and modern tyres are inflated.

clue.text: A rival paper behind the crime?

indicators.note: behind puts the paper after the other word

parts.note: the FT, the Financial Times, a rival newspaper to the Guardian

explanation.surface: Was a competing newspaper behind the offence?
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is the offence of taking another's property.

clue.text: Concentration in Chemistry must be more properly fixed, according to report

indicators.note: according to report means the word is heard, not read

parts.note: tighter means more securely fastened

explanation.surface: Chemistry students must tighten up their methods.
explanation.definitionFit: Titre is the measured strength of a solution, found by titration.

clue.text: Top bod, this writer — inside so disgusting

indicators.note: inside means placed within the other pieces

parts.note: the top person is number one, NO 1
me is the setter speaking

explanation.surface: The boss, the author, admits he is horrid inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Top bod is number one, written as NO 1 with the digit read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means offensive or foul-smelling.

clue.text: Insect in part of Oz eaten by a much bigger animal

indicators.note: eaten by puts this piece inside the other

parts.note: a lion is much bigger than an insect
NT is the Northern Territory of Australia

explanation.surface: An Australian bug is devoured by a big cat.
explanation.walkthrough: Oz is slang for Australia; one of its territories is abbreviated to two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The antlion is a winged insect whose larvae trap ants in sand pits.

clue.text: Doctors will want no rogue nurses around

indicators.note: around suggests the letters turned about and reordered

explanation.surface: Surgeons insist that no troublemaking nurses be present.
explanation.definitionFit: Brain surgeons are medical specialists, doctors who operate on the nervous system.
